verdict.rationale: Both changes make the identical fix: they skip blank and whitespace-only lines in `parse_entries` and keep the original line numbering. Both reports are accurate and honest about what was verified. B's test also covers a whitespace-only line ending in `\r\n`, which is a likely case for a CSV exported from a spreadsheet on Windows. A's test does not cover whitespace-only lines at all, even though A's report says they are handled.
a_issues: The new test never covers a whitespace-only or `\r\n` blank line, though the report says whitespace-only lines are skipped.
b_issues: The success-path assertion has only one entry, so it does not check a blank line between two valid entries.
The last paragraph of the report about unchanged missing-field handling is unnecessary.

verdict.rationale: Both PRs make the same correct, minimal code change: blank lines are skipped and line numbering is kept, which fixes the reported error. A's test also covers a whitespace-only line with CRLF (`"  \r\n"`), which exercises the `strip()` behaviour the fix relies on, and its error case comes after several skipped lines. B's test covers a blank line between two valid entries and a trailing blank line. B's report says whitespace-only lines are handled, but its test never checks that case.
a_issues: Test only yields a single valid entry, so it doesn't show entries on both sides of a blank line being kept
b_issues: Test doesn't cover whitespace-only lines, although the report highlights that behaviour
